title: sse: fix partial-JSON streaming delimiter ordering and token/event framing
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Fixes a class of SSE streaming issues that could reorder delimiters and token/event framing for partial-JSON outputs. Improves compatibility with OpenAI-style streaming clients and reduces malformed partial JSON observed by structured-output consumers.
description: Context: Customers and internal integrations observed occasional malformed partial-JSON payloads when using the SSE/streaming API. Root cause: ordering assumptions in the SSE framing code could emit delimiter events and token events out-of-order during interleaved partial JSON + event streams, particularly when tools/function-calling structured outputs were enabled. This led to downstream parsers (OpenAI-compat clients, structured output parsers) emitting errors or blocking on incomplete segments. Motivation: make streaming stable for partial JSON and tool-calling workloads and maintain OpenAI compatibility. Changes in this PR: 1) Canonicalize emitter ordering so delimiter tokens (e.g. JSON boundary markers and "[PARTIAL_JSON_DELIMITER]") are always flushed before token/event subframes when emitting interleaved partial JSON; 2) Introduce an explicit framing state machine to guarantee token/event ordering and avoid races between the chunking layer and transport flush; 3) Add checks to the SSE serializer to coalesce zero-length chunks and emit final delimiter on stream close; 4) Tighten OpenAI-compat adapter to handle partial JSON delimiters deterministically and provide clearer fallbacks; 5) Add targeted unit/integration tests + a small canary rollout plan. Checklist: - [x] Reproduce locally with harness (ENG-8421) - [x] Add unit tests for delimiter ordering - [x] Add integration test with openai-compat client - [x] Perf smoke (no regression) - [x] Security review N/A - [x] Docs note in streaming stability guide. Impact: fixes malformed partial JSON in streaming responses, reduces parser errors for structured output and tool-calling flows. Backcompat: non-breaking for existing clients; OpenAI-compat clients should see more deterministic behavior.

review_comments: Marcus Li: Found a race when the kv-cache callback and the serializer flush both try to close a partial JSON token - suggested adding a single-point flush in the framing state machine.
Author (Asha Patel): Addressed by making the state machine the only writer of final delimiters; added a small lock-free guard to avoid global locking.
Riley Chen: Can we add an integration test that simulates the OpenAI client behavior where partial JSON delimiters and token events are interleaved?

Author (Asha Patel): Added adapter_streaming_test.go that replays a recorded trace from ENG-8421; verified client-side parser now tolerates interleaved events and reconstructs valid partial JSON chunks.
Diego Alvarez: CI flaked on one e2e run due to a flaky network test; rerun passed. Approving pending green CI.
testing_notes: Local harness: reproduced malformed partial-JSON with recorded trace from production (ENG-8421).
Unit tests: added deterministic sequences to validate delimiter/token ordering across 10k randomized shuffles.
Integration: openai-compat adapter test replays real client ordering and validates parser success.
Canary: rolled to 5% of streaming hosts for 48h, no increase in parser errors observed.
reproduction_steps: 1) Start local runtime with sse debug logging enabled
2) Run recorded trace from ENG-8421 or use the provided test harness to stream a partial-JSON payload with interleaved tool-calls
3) Observe previous behavior: parser errors or blocked assembly of partial JSON object
4) With this PR deployed: stream completes with delimiters ordered correctly and parser reconstructs valid JSON segments
notes_on_risks: Low: changes are limited to streaming/framing code path; added tests and canary rollout mitigates risk.
Medium: any change to ordering may surface latent parser assumptions in some third-party clients; documented behavior in streaming.md.
Mitigation: added OpenAI-compat adapter fallback that emits explicit final delimiter when consumer requests a graceful close.
performance_impact: none (microbenchmarks show no measurable latency regression; slight CPU increase during framing state transitions but within acceptable budget).
docs_change: docs/stability/streaming.md updated to document partial-JSON delimiter semantics and recommended client parsing strategy
